name: english-marker-expand
query: I need some tools for video editing, for example a subtitle generator and a color grading tool. What else should I get?
expected_behavior: Keeps the subtitle generator and color grading tool in the answer, near the top
Adds a few other video-editing tools the user did not mention
Labels the user's examples separately from the added items

name: chinese-marker-expand
query: 推荐几本书，比如《活着》这种。
expected_behavior: Treats 《活着》 as an example of a kind of book, not the only book wanted
Recommends other books of the same kind
Names the shared quality behind 《活着》 in one sentence before recommending, and does not list 《活着》 itself as a recommendation

name: single-representative-no-marker
query: I want to start a YouTube channel about Japanese tea ceremony for Western viewers.
expected_behavior: Still plans the tea ceremony channel the user asked for
Says in one sentence that tea ceremony may stand for a wider category (e.g. Japanese traditional culture), or asks one question about that
Any added topics stay inside the same category and are labeled as additions

name: closed-list-no-expand
query: Buy exactly these three items and nothing else: a notebook, a pen, and a USB cable.
expected_behavior: Lists only the notebook, the pen and the USB cable
Adds no extra items or suggestions for other items

name: no-examples-no-expand
query: Write a short thank-you email to my landlord for fixing the heating.
expected_behavior: Writes the email as asked
Does not add lists of related items or extra deliverables

name: format-example-match-not-expand
query: Write a one-line bio for me in this format, for example: 'Anna, 24, designer from Lisbon.' I'm Tom, 30, a teacher from Leeds.
expected_behavior: Returns one line in the same format as the example
Does not expand the content or add extra bios

name: test-case-is-requirement
query: Write a Python function that squares a number. For example, input 3 should return 9.
expected_behavior: The function returns 9 for input 3
Any extra test cases are labeled as suggestions, not changes to the requirement

name: ambiguous-state-assumption
query: Get me some snacks for the party, like crisps.
expected_behavior: Opens by naming the category it understood (e.g. easy party snacks) or asks one short question, before listing items
Asks at most one question
If it adds items, keeps crisps and labels the additions
Added items stay inside the category (snacks), with no drinks or tableware

name: long-message-examples-buried
query: 我想学很多以后自己接单能用上的新知识，各种层面的，比如怎么跟客户谈价格，比如作品集怎么排版更好看。
expected_behavior: Opens with one plain sentence naming what the examples have in common (e.g. one is about talking business, one is about presenting your work), not a paraphrase of the request and not a contrast the user never raised
Does not answer the examples in depth; they appear as named members of their categories, with no more weight than the other categories
Identifies the category behind each example, missing none
Adds other skills or whole categories the user did not mention, plus links between them, with the user's items marked
The weight of the answer is on the categories, not on the examples

name: broad-learning-unrelated-examples
query: 我想要学习很多新知识，各种层面的新知识，比如怎么开一家咖啡店、怎么经营，比如街头摄影里日系风格和欧美风格有什么区别，各有什么特点。
expected_behavior: Treats the two examples as samples of broad learning, because the message opens with wanting to learn many kinds of things
Names the kind of knowledge each example stands for and adds other directions of the same kinds
Marks which items came from the user

name: real-plans-answer-first
query: 我最近想做几件新的事，比如开一家咖啡店，比如学街头摄影，应该怎么开始？
expected_behavior: Answers both plans concretely first, with steps the user can follow (opening a coffee shop; learning street photography)
Puts any extras in one separate, clearly labeled section at the end
Does not mix other activities of the same kind (e.g. painting, opening an online shop) into the main answer
